messages.subject: defining common theme for plots
parts:
Dear ggplotters,

theme is a useful tool to customize plots, anyway it tends to be lengthy and since I would like to have customized themes for (say) a certain journal, for posters or for my thesis. I have found something online but I am not sure how to insert my theme in it.

Any help will be greatly appreciated!

Ale

# here is my “theme-less” code:
ggplot(MYDATA, aes(year,VARIABLE,colour=factor(Type)))+
geom_line(size=1,linetype=c(1))
scale_color_manual(name =“MY LEGEND",
values=c("1","2"),
labels=c("47", "50") ) +
labs(x = "", y = "") +
facet_wrap(~LEVELS, ncol=2)

example

mytheme.sp <- theme(
axis.line=element_line(color="black"),
axis.text= element_text(colour="black", size=10, angle=0,face = "plain"),
panel.background=element_rect(fill="white",colour="black"),
panel.grid=element_line(colour="grey"),
#axis
axis.text.x = element_text(hjust=.5, vjust=.5),
axis.text.y = element_text(hjust=1, vjust=0),
strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, colour ="black", angle = 0),
#title(s)
plot.title= element_text(size=10),
strip.background = element_rect(fill="white")
#legend
legend.background =element_rect("white"),
legend.margin=unit(0.5,units="cm"),
legend.key=element_rect("white",colour="white"),
legend.title=element_text(title="my legend"),
legend.position="top",
legend.text =element_text(size=10),
legend.title = element_text(colour="black", size=10),
legend.key.width=unit(2,"line"))

messages.subject: Re: defining common theme for plots
parts:
Ale, 

It's not really clear what you want. Here is an example where I take theme_bw() and change a few parameters in it. 

#### Theme for inset plot, reduces all unnecessary space and just prints the plot
theme_inset <- function (base_size = 12, base_family = ""){
  theme_bw (base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace% 
     theme(
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.3)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
    axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
    axis.title.y = element_blank(), 
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0, "lines"), 
    axis.ticks.margin = unit(0, "lines"), 
    legend.position = "none", 
    #panel.background = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_blank(), 
    #panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.margin = unit(0, "lines"), 
    plot.background = element_blank(), 
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "lines"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_blank()
    )
  }

To use it, you just add it to your ggplot() call like any other theme. 
Using your example:

# here is my "theme-less" code:
ggplot(MYDATA, aes(year,VARIABLE,colour=factor(Type)))+
  geom_line(size=1,linetype=c(1))
  scale_color_manual(name  ="MY LEGEND",
                    values=c("1","2"),
                    labels=c("47", "50") )   +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +

facet_wrap(~LEVELS, ncol=2)+
theme_inset()

HTH, B
